title: Erinbrook Drive traffic safety and community centre expansion
subtitle: Also green development standards, community grants, a Francis Street South zoning change and the 2022 election review.
overview: The committee recommended new traffic safety measures on Erinbrook Drive after two severe collisions: all-way stops at The Country Way and Rockwood Road, two speed cushions, and a pedestrian crossover study near a trail and school connection {{vote:m5}}. It also recommended that the Mill Courtland Community Centre expansion move to detailed design {{vote:m4}}, with staff to return to Council if the budget cannot cover critical needs.

Other recommendations include starting Phase 2 of a harmonized regional green development standard {{vote:m3}}, approving 2023 Tier 2 community grants {{vote:m1}}, and lifting a holding provision at 30 Francis Street South {{vote:m2}}. These items go to Council for a final decision.

The committee also discussed the 2022 municipal election overview, which was an information item with no motion. Members indicated support for continued advocacy to the Province through the Association of Municipalities of Ontario for a unified approach to running municipal elections. A separate report on voting methods is expected in 2024.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended all-way stops at The Country Way and Rockwood Road, two speed cushions, a Uniform Traffic By-law amendment, and a pedestrian crossover study that could lead to a raised crosswalk, with staff to report back.
The committee received the business case for information and directed staff to move the expansion project to the detailed design phase.
The committee received the report and recommended that staff start Phase 2 of the harmonized green development standards project and bring a recommendation back to Council.
The committee recommended approving $198,137 in Tier 2 community grants and moving several named organizations to the Tier 1 process for 2024.
The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment that removes Holding Provision 90H from the lands.

debate: On Erinbrook Drive, staff said the measures were chosen using speed and collision data, and that all-way stops mainly manage right-of-way rather than calm traffic. A councillor relayed resident concerns that the measures might not go far enough, and staff committed to follow-up data collection and further measures if needed.

A councillor asked for a pedestrian crossover or raised crosswalk on the section near the trail and school connection. Staff said speeds there were lower but agreed to study it when trail use is higher and report back.

On green development standards, members asked about costs, effects on housing affordability and approval times. The consultant said upfront costs may rise but life-cycle savings offset them. One councillor urged a balance with affordability, and another asked whether the standards could be required for smaller developments, which staff said was still to be determined.

On Mill Courtland, members asked about the gap between the business case cost and the budget, how long the centre would be closed, and whether to build larger given expected neighbourhood growth. Staff said critical elements would be prioritized with neighbourhood associations, temporary program locations were being explored, and a smaller centre better serves the neighbourhood.

On the 2022 election, members and a delegate discussed voter outreach, the case for allowing election signs on roadsides, how many races appear on one ballot, and candidates running on issues outside municipal responsibility.
